text:
anjali: Heads up — sketching a 'sustaining base + transient capacity' approach for GPU fleets. Spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1example (WIP). TL;DR: keep a small steady on-demand base per region for latency-sensitive routes, plus transient preemptible/spot pools for cost efficiency. Need quick opinions on floor sizing, routing level, and interruption handling.

mike_g: Looks sensible. What's the proposed base %? 10–20%? Also how do we differentiate saturation vs a price-driven eviction wave?

anjali: Thinking ~15% of forecasted peak per model family as a starting point, tuned by qps + p95 latency. Detection: combine market price signal + runtime signals (eviction rate, queue depth, tail latency). If evictionRate > threshold OR p95 > SLA we move traffic.

sara: Are we mixing at the request-router or at infra (k8s node pools)? Concern: tiny base might cause cold-start latency.

kevin: Prefer routing-layer mix. Keep a warm „base" pool with small VMs so kernel / caches stay hot. Also pin a tiny number of long-lived nodes per shard to keep KV cache warm and avoid model-load cold starts.

mike_g: Proposed autoscaler snippet for discussion:
```
minReplicas: ceil(0.15 * forecast_peak)
maxReplicas: forecast_peak
scalePolicy: preferOnDemandUntilThreshold
priceFallback: true
```
Also: label/taint transient nodes with capacity=transient so the scheduler and router can treat them differently.

anjali: For interruption handling I want a graceful handoff path: detect eviction -> internal reroute to on-demand variant if available -> if not, push small amount into queue with token-bucket to limit thundering herd, and optionally return a soft-failure that triggers client-side retry. Prefer internal reroute over direct 503s for user-facing latency.

infra-bot: incident: spot-eviction-spike detected in us-west-2 at 1856123500. Eviction rate 12% in last 5m.

sara: :eyes: That matches our load test window. Can we pre-warm +2 on-demand nodes from the reserve buffer (charge to burst-fund) and steer high-SLO traffic there?

kevin: Yes. Add policy: if evictionRate > 5% AND p95_latency > configured_threshold -> allocate reservePool up to +10% for 10 minutes. Tag all allocations with billing_label=burst-fund. Emit alert for cost owner.

mike_g: One risk: correlated spikes across regions could exhaust reservePool. Suggest multi-tier fallback: 1) prioritize by route SLO, 2) fallback to cheaper model variants (quantized/gpt-small), 3) use reserve pool, 4) graceful degradation. Also consider a global budget throttle for burst-fund.

anjali: Agree. Action items: update RFC with simulation numbers (cost vs availability curves), add autoscaler policy examples, and add fallback ordering. I'll post a PR for the RFC later today. Thanks all!

anjali: Filing RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/123
